question.text: What is a CAS (Consolidated Account Statement) in the context of mutual fund investments?

answer.text: A statement showing only mutual fund holdings from a single AMC
A single statement consolidating an investor's mutual fund and demat holdings across all AMCs, sent monthly if transactions occurred or half-yearly otherwise
A statement issued only on investor request through the AMC
A statement showing only the capital gains and tax details of investments

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series II-B workbook (pp.187-188, 193), AMCs and RTAs share investor data with depositories so a single Consolidated Account Statement can be generated. Depositories dispatch the CAS for PANs common to demat and AMC/RTA records (monthly when transactions occur, half-yearly otherwise). Where there is no demat account, AMCs/RTAs send the CAS, and RTAs also issue MF-only consolidated statements across AMCs/RTAs. The Trap: CAS is not AMC-specific — that's an individual account statement from each AMC. It is not issued only on request. Note: Distinguish the dispatch paths: depositories send the combined CAS where demat and MF records overlap; AMCs/RTAs send the MF-only CAS where there is no demat account.
